description.value: Oomomo Japan Living is a Japanese lifestyle variety store on Robson Street carrying a wide range of imported Japanese goods including health and beauty products, stationery, kitchenware, houseware, apparel, and collectibles. It also stocks a selection of Japanese food and drinks — snacks, candy, tea, coffee, and seasonings — making it a useful stop for specialty provisions. The store is wheelchair accessible according to OSM.

bike_parking_detail: 6 racks within 100m: stands (2 spaces) at 25m; stands (2 spaces) at 30m; rack (5 spaces) at 32m; rack (5 spaces) at 43m; stands (2 spaces) at 54m; stands (4 spaces) at 81m. Total: 20 spaces.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website confirms Oomomo is a real, operating Japanese lifestyle/variety store selling health & beauty, stationery, kitchenware, houseware, apparel, toys, and a food & drinks section (snacks, candy, tea, etc.). OSM tag toilets=no is used as evidence for Washrooms=false, as the website provides no contradicting information. No evidence exists in OSM tags or website content for bike parking, water refill, or most other cyclist amenities; the food & drinks section carries snack-type items rather than basic grocery staples.
concerns: OSM matched_tag_value is 'department_store' but the record is categorized as 'Groceries'; the business is primarily a Japanese lifestyle/variety store and would be better categorized as General Retail or Specialty Retail.
Website content retrieved is almost entirely navigation menus with minimal store-specific detail; contact page did not surface a phone number or address for cross-verification.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Real, open, publicly accessible retail store on a major Vancouver street; confirmed active via website and recent OSM check_date of 2024-09-18. Category mismatch noted but does not warrant exclusion as the store does carry food items.

provenance.category_correction_reason: OSM tags this as a department_store, and the website confirms it is primarily a Japanese lifestyle/variety store (health & beauty, stationery, kitchenware, houseware, toys) with a secondary food & drinks section selling snacks, candy, and tea. It is not primarily a grocery store; a category of General Retail or Specialty Retail would be more accurate.

Basic groceries.detail: Store carries a Food & Drinks section (candy, chocolate, coffee, cookies, drinks, rice crackers, snacks, tea) but no evidence of staple groceries such as produce, dairy, or bread
